newsitem.title: USA: Greepeace to ask court to stop Arco drilling in Arctic.
newsitem.headline: Greepeace to ask court to stop Arco drilling in Arctic.

text.p: The environmental group Greenpeace said Tuesday it planned to file suit against Los Angeles-based Atlantic Richfield Co. to stop one of the oil giant's rigs from drilling in the Arctic Ocean.

Meanwhile, Greenpeace protesters and ships were camped on a small island near the rig off the coast of Alaska and Arco said it feared that they might try to interfere with the drilling, scheduled to start in November. The rig is now at the giant Prudhoe Bay oil field about 75 miles east of the planned drilling site.
Arco has sent a representative to meet with the group and ask them not to disrupt operations.

Greenpeace said it will ask a federal court here on Wednesday to issue a temporary restraining order to prevent Arco from moving a mobile rig to the Beaufort Sea off the northern coast of Alaska. Greenpeace said that Arco had not obtained a permit required to move the rig to the site.
The move is part of Greenpeace's larger campaign to stop oil exploration in the Artic and the North Atlantic.
"We're trying to use every means possible to stop the rig being used, and to stop their exploration plans," said Paul Horsman, a member of Greenpeace involved in the lawsuit.
Arco says obtaining a permit is voluntary but it is applying for one so as not to interfere with subsistence whaling hunters in the area.
"We are not in violation of the Marine Mammal Protection Act (as Greenpeace has charged)," an Arco spokesman said.
Arco says it must move the rig before winter ice blocks the journey.
"We expect any effort to interfere with our operations to be shortlived," the Arco spokesman said.
